title: State of the City 2026: From Realignment to Renaissance
description: Videos provided to you by the City of Santa Monica.

Santa Monica was originally intended to be a port city. Its founders built a warf thousands of feet long, imagined ship after ship docking at our W's edge, only for their dreams to be shipwrecked when Congress declared San Pedro as the port of Los Angeles. Their failure was the birth of a new kind of city, a coastal resort town, a dazzling pier that attracted thousands to its shores. Our town has fallen and been reborn more times than most may realize. In 2020, we saw the greatest shipwreck of all, a global pandemic that brought the world to its knees. Our ocean was sealed off with caution tape. But the waves kept crashing, doing the only thing they know how to do. Writing love notes to the moon and knowing with certainty that it would one day be high tide again. A new ship is headed to our shore. A mighty crew has built a port where we can dock and welcome home some of the dreams we once thought had been lost at sea. The ship's manifest is full of storytellers and librarians and poets, archivists and healers and activists. The voyage has been long and there is still much work to be done. May we roll up our pant legs and feel the salty water rush up to our knees. This is high tide at its finest. A city that wants to be reborn. A ship sailing the waters of our collective memory.
